slot.brief: A wire of given resistance is stretched so that its length increases by a factor n (volume constant); find the new resistance using R ∝ L², with the cross-section change handled implicitly.

stem: A wire has resistance $4\ \Omega$. It is stretched until its length is three times its original length, with its volume unchanged. What is its new resistance?

verdicts.working: At constant volume, tripling the length reduces the area to one-third. Since R = ρL/A, the new resistance is 4 × 3 × 3 = 36 Ω.

working:
With volume constant, $A'L'=AL$; thus $R'=\rho\dfrac{L'}{A'}=\rho\dfrac{(3L)(3A)}{A}=9R=36\ \Omega$.

Independent check: At constant volume, tripling the length reduces the area to one-third. Since R = ρL/A, the new resistance is 4 × 3 × 3 = 36 Ω.
